column1: # Incidents Blindspot checks for. One line each, tab separated. After editing, run: bash tools/gen.sh
#   id      what the other data files refer to
#   name    as the report shows it
#   impact  what it did, at most about 14 words, every word supported by the source
#   source  the primary source (vendor advisory, GitHub advisory, CISA or a named research post)
#   level   act: treat the machine as compromised. update: update the version; the machine itself is not compromised.
#           leak: a hosted platform leaked what people stored on it (data/platforms.tsv names the incident, and
#           only a platform's incident is a leak): rotate what was stored there; never a compromised machine
#   advice  optional: one more fix, shown in What to do when a package or extension of the incident
#           is found (bad-npm, bad-pypi, bad-extensions; gen.sh refuses it on any other incident). An
#           update-level incident's advice comes right after the act-now fixes
#   summary optional, only for an update-level incident with advice: summary row 05 when the incident
#           is the most urgent thing section 5 found, at most 49 characters (row 05's room at 80 columns)
